label: Transient gap-junction blockade makes planarian fragments build heads of other species
claim: Temporary exposure of planarian fragments to a blocker of electrical synapses (gap junctions) causes them to build head shapes of other planarian species 100–150 million years distant, with no genetic change; Levin interprets this as the bioelectric network navigating to other attractors in morphospace, and the worms later remodel back to normal.
quote: One example of this plasticity of morphogenetic behavior (expanding on the default genetically encoded repertoire) is the fact that temporary exposure to a blocker of electrical synapses (i.e., an anesthetic) causes planarian fragments to create the heads of other species, with no genetic change required (Emmons-Bell et al. 2015; Sullivan et al. 2016).
paper_title: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
section: Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity
scope: Planarian flatworms (Girardia dorotocephala and related species), author's lab (Emmons-Bell et al. 2015)

label: Newt kidney tubules keep normal diameter with fewer, larger cells, down to one cell
claim: In newts whose embryonic cells are made larger (e.g. by polyploidy), kidney tubules use fewer cells to keep the normal tubule diameter and body size, and with enormous cells a single cell bends around itself to form the tubule, showing that different molecular mechanisms are called on to reach the same large-scale anatomical goal.
quote: However, if the cells of the early embryo are artificially made to be larger, fewer cells will be used, resulting in the same (normal) tubule diameter and overall body size. Remarkably, this can be pushed to a fascinating extreme: if the cells are made to be enormous, a single cell will bend around itself, producing the normal size tubule diameter.
paper_title: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
section: Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity
scope: Polyploid newt embryos (Fankhauser 1945)

label: Xenobots perform kinematic self-replication not known in any other species
claim: Xenobots, proto-organisms that form spontaneously from dissociated frog embryo skin cells, are motile via cilia and perform kinematic self-replication, building copies of themselves from loose cells in the medium, a novel solution reached within 48 h without any evolutionary history of selection as Xenobots.
quote: The most remarkable novel behavior is that of kinematic self-replication: Xenobots build copies of themselves by rearranging loose cells provided to them in the medium. This is Von Neumann-style replication that is not, to our knowledge, used by any other species on Earth.
paper_title: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
section: Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity
scope: Xenobots made from Xenopus laevis embryonic ectoderm (Kriegman et al. 2021a)

label: Scrambled Xenopus tadpole faces reach a normal frog face by new paths
claim: During metamorphosis, Xenopus laevis tadpoles reach the correct frog face configuration not only from a normal tadpole configuration but also from a wide range of experimentally scrambled craniofacial configurations, using new paths through morphospace that end in the same goal region.
quote: For example, during metamorphosis, the tadpole of Xenopus laevis can reach the correct frog face region of morphospace not only from its default starting position (a normal tadpole configuration), but also from a wide range of scrambled configurations (Vandenberg et al. 2012)—using new paths through that morphospace that nevertheless end up in the same goal region (Friston et al. 2015; Pezzulo and Levin 2016).
paper_title: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
section: Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Navigation: an invariant between morphological, behavioral, and other spaces
scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles with induced craniofacial malformations (author's lab, Vandenberg et al. 2012)

label: A few bioelectrically induced lens cells recruit host cells to build a normal-sized lens
claim: When an ectopic lens is induced in tail tissue by bioelectric modulation, misexpressing the ion channel in only a small subset of the needed cells suffices: these cells recruit unmodified host cells to reach the critical mass for a normal-sized lens, so downstream modules such as size control are activated without micromanagement.
quote: For example, when an ectopic lens (in tail tissue) is induced by bioelectric modulation, it is sufficient to misexpress the channel only in a small subset of the needed cells: once their organ-level goal is specified, these cells will secondarily recruit other (un-modified) host cells as needed to achieve the critical mass needed to produce a normal-sized lens.
paper_title: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
section: Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Navigation: an invariant between morphological, behavioral, and other spaces
scope: Xenopus laevis embryos with ion channel misexpression in tail tissue

label: Gap junctions wipe ownership of memory molecules, partly erasing cell individuality
claim: By directly connecting the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells, gap junctions provide an 'owner wiping property' for stress signals and other molecular traces of experience (e.g. calcium flux), so cells cannot tell whether such a signal is their own or a neighbour's; this partly erases individual cell identity and lets the collective scale up measurements, stored goals and actions.
quote: Second, by providing direct connections between the intracellular milieus of cells, they provide an “owner wiping property” for stress signals and other molecular traces of experience: cells cannot tell whether a given memory molecule (e.g., calcium flux) belongs to itself or its neighbors.
paper_title: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind
section: Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › E pluribus unum
scope: Gap-junction-coupled cells in morphogenetic and neural tissues

label: Single adult human lung cells self-construct into motile multicellular biobots
claim: A single normal human bronchial epithelial cell from adult lung, cultured in extracellular matrix for two weeks and then transferred to a low-viscosity medium, self-constructs into a multicellular, motile spheroid (an Anthrobot) without genetic editing, scaffolds or manual sculpting.
quote: Each Anthrobot begins as a single cell, derived from the adult human lung, and self‐constructs into a multicellular motile biobot after being cultured in extra cellular matrix for 2 weeks and transferred into a minimally viscous habitat.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Abstract
scope: Normal human bronchial epithelial (NHBE) progenitor cells from adult donors, in vitro

label: Morphogenetic plasticity is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cells
claim: The ability of adult, somatic, genetically wild-type human cells to form a novel functional anatomy with new behaviours shows that the plasticity seen in Xenobots is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cells, and is a fundamental feature of wild-type cells that needs no direct genetic manipulation to unlock.
quote: The ability of adult, somatic, human cells to form a novel functional anatomy, with unique behaviors, reveals that this plasticity is not restricted to amphibian or embryonic cell properties, and is a fundamental feature of wild‐type cells that requires no direct genetic manipulation to unlock.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Introduction
scope: Genetically wild-type cells generally, generalized from adult human airway epithelium and Xenopus embryonic cells

label: Lower viscosity may drive apical-out polarity reversal of airway spheroids
claim: The authors hypothesize that airway spheroids keep cilia in the lumen because basal cells interact with the surrounding high-viscosity matrix, and that moving spheroids to a lower-viscosity, water-based medium may trigger basal cells to migrate inward so the ciliated apical layer takes their place on the spheroid surface.
quote: Given that cilia naturally localize into the lumen due to the basal cells’ interaction with the surrounding high‐viscosity matrix, we hypothesized that changing the culture environment to a lower viscosity level (e.g., water‐based media instead of gel‐based matrix) may trigger the basal layer cells to migrate inward and allow the apical layer to take their place on the spheroid cortex.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
scope: Human bronchial epithelial spheroids grown in Matrigel and transferred to low-adhesive liquid culture

label: Apical-in spheroids become motile within a week in low-adhesive liquid culture
claim: Human bronchial epithelial spheroids that are apical-in and non-motile on release from Matrigel become motile by day 7 in low-adhesive liquid culture, with beating cilia on their outer surface; immunostaining shows a large increase in external multiciliated cells between day 0 and day 7.
quote: This new approach has enabled the originally apical‐in spheroids (that show no motility on day 0 as shown on Figure 1b.1) to became motile by day 7 (Figure 1b.2), featuring highly motile ciliary appendages on the spheroid surface.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
scope: NHBE-derived spheroids in vitro, Anthrobot protocol with retinoic acid

label: Higher culture viscosity reduces Anthrobot motility and size
claim: Culturing Anthrobots in environments more viscous than the protocol baseline decreases both their motility and their size, suggesting that low-viscosity environments favour the growth of functional, larger bots.
quote: We observed that culture environments with higher viscosity levels than the protocol baseline result in decreased motility (Figure S2, Supporting Information) and size (Figure S3, Supporting Information), suggesting that low‐viscosity environments better facilitate the growth of functional bots as well as yield larger bots.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in vitro

label: Initial cell seeding density is a control knob for Anthrobot size and maturation
claim: Changing the initial seeding density of bronchial epithelial cells in Matrigel (half, default or double 30,000 cells/mL) significantly changes the resulting Anthrobot sizes and the time course of motility, though not linearly, suggesting that seeding density is a tractable control parameter for Anthrobot morphology and function.
quote: These results show that the size and time course of maturation of motile bots could be modulated by altering the concentration of cells in the Anthrobot differentiation culture, suggesting initial cell seeding density to be a tractable control knob for Anthrobot morphology and function.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in vitro, seeding densities 15,000–60,000 cells/mL

label: Anthrobot motility onset follows a sigmoidal time course peaking around day 10
claim: After release from the matrix, the number of motile Anthrobots rises along a sigmoidal curve over three weeks, with the largest change in motility on day 10, and this rise reflects a morphological reorganization that exposes cilia on the surface.
quote: To characterize the temporal dynamics of motility initiation, we periodically (every other day) counted the number of motile spheroids for 3 weeks following dissolution and observed a sigmoidal motility profile with peak change in motility on day 10 (Figure 1C).
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in vitro, first 3 weeks after matrix dissolution

label: Anthrobot motility is cilia-driven
claim: Blocking ciliary motion with ciliobrevin sharply decreases Anthrobot motility, showing that their locomotion is driven by surface cilia.
quote: We administered the efficient blocker of cilia motion, ciliobrevin,[ 20 ] and observed the expected drastic decrease in motility (See Figure S6, Supporting Information), confirming that the motility of Anthrobots is cilia‐driven.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in vitro

label: Anthrobot trajectories fall into four movement types
claim: Unsupervised clustering of 30-second trajectory segments from about 200 Anthrobots, described by straightness and gyration indices, yields four statistically distinct movement types: circular, linear, curvilinear and eclectic.
quote: Further investigation of these clusters reveals that each represents a distinct movement type: circular, linear, curvilinear and “eclectic” (Figure 2D).
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in low-adhesive dishes, 5-hour time-lapse tracking

label: Circular motion is the most stable Anthrobot behaviour; eclectic motion is transient
claim: In a Markov-chain model of transitions between movement types, circular motion is the most persistent Anthrobot behaviour, followed by linear and curvilinear motion, while eclectic motion acts as a transient intermediate that probabilistically resolves into one of the other three types.
quote: We observed that the most stable movement pattern for an Anthrobot is circular motion, followed by linear/curvilinear motion. The eclectics act more like an intermediate and over time, at least probabilistically, resolve into one of the 3 other categories.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots, 30 s trajectory segments over 5 h

label: Anthrobots self-organize into discrete, stable movement types with individual fingerprints
claim: Because Anthrobot movement types are highly consistent and rarely interconvert (for example between circular and linear), the authors conclude that Anthrobots self-organize into discrete, stable movement types, each bot having a distinct motility fingerprint.
quote: The fact that Anthrobots exhibit movement types with high “consistency” and low rates of inter‐type conversion (e.g., between circulars and linear) suggests that Anthrobots self‐organize into discrete and stable movement types, each bot having a distinct motility fingerprint.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Discrete Movement Types
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in vitro

label: Morphotype 2 is most ciliated; morphotype 3 has the most polarized cilia
claim: Among the three Anthrobot morphotypes, morphotype 2 (the largest and least regular) is significantly more ciliated than the other two, and morphotype 3 has a significantly more polarized, clustered cilia distribution with the fewest isolated cilia patches.
quote: These four indices together describe type 2 bots as being significantly more ciliated than type 1 and type 3 bots, and type 3 bots as having a significantly more polarized cilia distribution pattern (with the least amount of extra‐cluster noise) in comparison to type 1 and type 2 bots (Figure 3D).
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Distinct Morphological Types
scope: About 350 NHBE-derived Anthrobots

label: Anthrobots form three morphotypes, split first by size and shape, then by cilia pattern
claim: Principal component analysis and clustering of eight shape and cilia indices from about 350 Anthrobots yields three morphotypes, organized as a decision tree in which size and shape smoothness separate small, smooth spherical bots (morphotype 1) from larger, irregular bots, which are then split by cilia pattern into non-polarized (morphotype 2) and polarized (morphotype 3).
quote: In summary, our morphological characterization pipeline suggest that Anthrobots self‐organize into 3 major morphotypes (Figure 3E) and this relationship can be represented by a developmental decision tree shown on Figure 3F wherein the first “decision point” determines the Anthrobot size and shape.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Distinct Morphological Types
scope: About 350 NHBE-derived Anthrobots imaged by confocal microscopy

label: Non-movers, linear and circular bots map onto morphotypes 1, 2 and 3
claim: Anthrobot behaviour and morphology are significantly associated: non-moving bots fall mostly in morphotype 1 (small, smooth, spherical), linear movers mostly in morphotype 2 (large, non-polarized cilia) and circular movers mostly in morphotype 3 (polarized cilia), and no displacing bot was found in morphotype 1.
quote: We have further computed the statistical significance of these overlaps (using the Fisher test, see Materials and Methods) and conclude that the non‐movers, linear, and circulars significantly correspond with the morphotypes 1, 2 and 3, respectively.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Distinct Movement Types and Morphotypes are Highly Correlated
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots; 350 imaged bots of which 28 had assigned displacing movement types

label: Spherical bots with uniform cilia may not move because ciliary forces cancel
claim: Morphotype 1 Anthrobots are likely non-movers or stationary wigglers, which the authors suggest may be because their radially symmetric spherical shape with evenly distributed cilia makes ciliary propulsion forces cancel out, with small imbalances producing only wiggling.
quote: This may be attributable to their spherical shape with homogeneously distributed cilia where the propulsion forces generated by the ciliary motion are more prone to canceling each other out due to the radially symmetric spherical shape, resulting in little or no movement.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Distinct Movement Types and Morphotypes are Highly Correlated
scope: Small, spherical, uniformly ciliated Anthrobots (morphotype 1)

label: Linear-moving Anthrobots are more bilaterally symmetric about their movement axis
claim: Linear-moving Anthrobots show higher bilateral symmetry of cilia distribution about their axis of movement than circular movers; for circular bots, but not linear bots, the 90-degree rotated axis is more symmetric than the movement axis (p = 0.048), supporting distinct local symmetry profiles for distinct movement types.
quote: Taken together, these findings support our hypothesis that Anthrobots with distinct movement types have distinct local bilateral symmetry profiles, with linear bots showing higher bilateral symmetry.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis
scope: 28 displacing NHBE-derived Anthrobots (15 circular, 13 linear)

label: Anthrobots recapitulate the bilateral symmetry of many wild-type species
claim: The link between straight-line movement and bilateral symmetry in Anthrobots suggests that these synthetic forms, self-assembling in a symmetrical environment, recapitulate a fundamental morphological property seen in many wild-type species and could be used to study how embryos establish a single body midplane.
quote: This suggests that these synthetic forms recapitulate a fundamental morphological property observed in many wild‐type species.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Show Bilateral Asymmetry Along Movement Axis
scope: Anthrobots compared with bilaterally symmetric animals

label: Faster and more rotational Anthrobots cover more of a neuronal scratch
claim: Anthrobots can move across scratches in human neuronal monolayers in vitro, and bots with higher rotational tendency or higher speed cover a larger proportion of unique positions along the scratch interface.
quote: Taken together, these data reveal that Anthrobots are capable of efficiently moving across damaged tissues, and that bots that have a higher rotational tendency and or higher speed have higher degrees of unique coordinate coverage by moving across a higher percentage of the scratch interface.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in scratched monolayers of hiNSC-derived human neurons, n = 17 bots

label: An intermediate gyration maximizes how closely Anthrobots track scratch edges
claim: In a constrained set of 13 Anthrobots in neuronal scratches, gyration (rotational tendency) has a quadratic relationship with how closely a bot's trajectory follows the scratch edge (p = 0.006), suggesting an intermediate gyration range maximizes edge tracking.
quote: With our constrained dataset, we saw that gyration had a quadratic effect on scratch‐trajectory similarity (Figure 5E) with p = 0.006, suggesting that there is a specific range for gyration where the scratch‐trajectory correlation can be maximized
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Can Move Across Scratches on Live Monolayers In Vitro
scope: 13 NHBE-derived Anthrobots with rotational tendency 0.33–0.7 in hiNSC-derived neuronal scratches

label: Superbot bridges induce neuronal gap closure in scratched monolayers
claim: Fused Anthrobot assemblies (superbots) placed across a scratch in a human neuronal monolayer induce substantial regrowth of neuronal tissue beneath them within 72 hours, forming a stitch that connects the two sides of the scratch.
quote: Strikingly, within the next 72 h upon inoculation of the superbot into the tissue scratch on day 0, we observed a substantial regrowth of the native tissue taking place (i.e., gap closure), resulting in the formation of a stitch right underneath the “superbot bridge,” connecting the two sides of the scratch (Figure 6B).
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues
scope: Superbots of fused NHBE-derived Anthrobots on scratched hiNSC-derived human neuronal monolayers in vitro

label: Superbot-induced gap closure is local and restores native tissue density
claim: Neuronal gap closure occurs only at the site where a superbot is placed; the neuronal coverage density there is statistically indistinguishable from intact tissue outside the scratch, while adjacent and distant parts of the scratch have significantly lower coverage.
quote: Thus, the density of the induced gap closure area that formed as a result of the presence of the superbot represented full (statistically indistinguishable from 100%) recovery of the original tissue and was uniquely different from the surrounding scratch area.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues
scope: Superbots on scratched hiNSC-derived human neuronal monolayers; bridges maintained over 3 days (5 of 10)

label: Passive mechanical loading does not reproduce Anthrobot-induced neural repair
claim: Placing a piece of agarose on neuronal scratches for 4 days to provide passive mechanical loading induces no repair, indicating that simple mechanical contact is not sufficient for the gap closure seen with Anthrobot superbots.
quote: Finally, in order to test whether simple (passive) mechanical contact was sufficient to induce the same effect, we incubated neuronal scratches for 4 days with a piece of agarose on top to provide mechanical loading; this induced no repair (see Figure S11, Supporting Information).
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues
scope: Scratched hiNSC-derived human neuronal monolayers in vitro

label: Anthrobots and Xenobots share similar movement types and transition profiles
claim: Anthrobots and Xenobots both show discrete movement types with very low interconversion between linear and circular motion (0.2% and 0.3% for Anthrobots, 0.5% and 1.6% for Xenobots) and highly consistent circular behaviour (92% and 95%), though Anthrobot linear behaviour is more consistent (80% versus 67%).
quote: The interconversion between linear and circular is very small for Xenobots (0.5% and 1.6%) and Anthrobots (0.2% and 0.3%), while their consistency of Circular behavior is extremely high for Xenobots (95%) just like for Anthrobots (92%).
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Discussion
scope: Human NHBE-derived Anthrobots compared with Xenopus laevis Xenobots

label: Similar forms from divergent genomes point to generic laws of morphogenesis
claim: Because Anthrobots and Xenobots, despite highly divergent genomes, ages and tissue origins, assemble into very similar kinds of motile constructs, the authors conclude that generic laws of morphogenesis matter in addition to species-specific genomic information.
quote: Despite their highly divergent genome, age, and tissue origin, the two platforms assemble into very similar types of creatures, illustrating the importance of generic laws of morphogenesis[ 31 ] in addition to species‐specific genomic information.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Discussion
scope: Self-assembling multicellular constructs from human and amphibian cells

label: Superbot size is set by bot number and fusion requires exposed basal layers
claim: Anthrobots fuse into larger superbots only in the days immediately after release from the matrix, while their basal layers are still exposed and can mediate bot-to-bot fusion, and superbot size can be controlled by the number of Anthrobots cultured together in a well.
quote: The tendency of the bots to fuse together and thus form different sized collectives (i.e., superbots) for different scratches can be controlled by modulating the number of Anthrobots cultured together in the same well for fusion, which happens only on days immediately following dissolution while the Anthrobot basal layers are still exposed and thus can mediate the bot‐to‐bot fusion.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Discussion
scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in the days after matrix dissolution

label: Tracheal cells healing neural tissue could not be predicted from current models
claim: That wild-type cells from the trachea move over and heal neural tissue is unexpected given their normal role in the body and could not be predicted from any current molecular or tissue-level model, which suggests screening engineered tissue interactions to uncover novel cell capabilities.
quote: The finding is unexpected given these tissues’ normal roles in the human body – the fact that wild‐type cells from trachea will move over and heal neural tissues could not be predicted from any current molecular or tissue‐level models.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Discussion
scope: Human airway epithelium-derived Anthrobots interacting with neural tissue

label: Patient-derived Anthrobots could be deployed in vivo without an immune response
claim: Because Anthrobots are made from adult human tissue, they could in future be personalized for each patient and deployed in that patient's body without triggering an immune response.
quote: Anthrobots are derived from adult human tissue, and in the future could be personalized for each patient, enabling safe in‐vivo deployment of these robots in the human body without triggering an immune response.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Discussion
scope: Autologous Anthrobots in human patients

label: Anthrobots may be made from other ciliated human cells such as oviduct or ependyma
claim: Anthrobots may be generable from other ciliated human cells, such as oviductal epithelium or brain ependymal cells, and non-ciliated cell types could be used for bots that need no autonomous motility.
quote: Anthrobots may be able to be generated from other ciliated cells in the human body (e.g., oviductal epithelia or brain ependymal cells), and other cell types can be used for bots when autonomous motility is not needed
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Conclusion
scope: Ciliated and non-ciliated adult human cell types

label: One genome yielding diverse forms in different environments could shape evolution
claim: The additional morphogenetic competencies revealed by Anthrobots could matter for evolutionary developmental biology, since the evolution of anatomical and functional features could be affected by the ability of the same genome to produce very diverse forms in different environments.
quote: More fundamentally, these data reveal additional morphogenetic competencies of cells which could have implications for evolutionary developmental biology, as evolution of anatomical and functional features could be affected by the ability of the same genome to produce very diverse forms in different environments.
paper_title: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells
section: Conclusion
scope: Evolution of anatomy in multicellular organisms

label: A collective's perceptual field and ability to find alternative paths grow with its size
claim: Extending William James' definition of intelligence (reaching the same goal by different means) to collectives via the perceptual field, the region of space and time an agent can survey for alternative paths to a goal, the authors propose that as a collective grows its perceptual field increases, improving its ability to find variant paths.
quote: As the size of a collective increases its perceptual field increases, improving its ability to find variant paths.
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction
scope: Cell collectives and other biological collectives

label: Neural unification into a self is a pivot of earlier morphogenetic cell communication
claim: It has been hypothesized, and the authors adopt, that the ability of neurons to unify into a centralized self is an evolutionary pivot of earlier cell-communication strategies that first solved problems in anatomical morphospace, a domain also requiring information processing above the single-cell level.
quote: Indeed it has been hypothesized that the remarkable ability of neurons to unify toward a centralized self – the emergent agent that is the subject of memories, preferences, and goals which are not assignable to any of the individual components – is an evolutionary pivot of far earlier cell communication strategies that first solved problems in navigating another domain that requires information processing above the single cell level: anatomical morphospace70.
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction
scope: Evolution of nervous systems from non-neural bioelectric signalling in metazoans

label: The number of embryos a blastoderm forms is not fixed by genetics
claim: The number of individuals formed by an embryonic blastoderm is not fixed at one by the genome: temporarily introducing breaks that informationally isolate islands of cells yields twins, triplets and so on, showing the blastoderm is an excitable medium in which several coherent embryos can self-organize.
quote: Indeed, the question of how many individuals are present in an embryonic blastoderm is not fixed at 1 by the genetics, because temporary introduction of breaks in the blastoderm (leading to informational isolation of islands of cell masses) results in twins, triplets, etc103.
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction › Development: transition to multicellularity
scope: Early vertebrate (e.g. avian) blastoderms

label: Keratocyte fragments migrate to the anode while whole keratocytes migrate to the cathode
claim: In an electric field, whole keratocytes migrate toward the cathode while fragments of keratocytes migrate toward the anode, so the collective (an intact cell) has the opposite taxis to its parts, illustrating that collective behaviour can be a hard-to-predict function of component tendencies.
quote: In an electric field, keratocytes migrate to the cathode, but fragments of keratocytes migrate to the anode104.
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction › Cell migration: the group does not go where each of the parts wants to go
scope: Fish keratocytes and keratocyte fragments in applied electric fields

label: Targeting instructor-cell voltage converts tadpole melanocytes to a melanoma-like state
claim: In Xenopus tadpoles, briefly targeting the bioelectric state of a small population of instructor cells (with a chloride channel activator or a GlyCl mutant), in the absence of carcinogens, oncogenes or DNA damage, converts melanocytes throughout the animal, including distant ones, into an over-proliferative, invasive melanoma-like phenotype via disruption of serotonergic signalling.
quote: This could be achieved in the absence of classical carcinogens, oncogenes, or DNA damage, by brief exposure to chemical (chloride ion channel activator drug) or molecular-genetic (GlyCl mutant) targeting of the bioelectric state of a specific cell population: instructor cells which normally keep the melanocytes in their healthy state via serotonergic signaling118.
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction › From normal melanocytes to a melanoma phenotype: a collective decision
scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles

label: Melanocyte conversion is all-or-none per animal, stochastic only across the cohort
claim: Melanocyte conversion after instructor-cell depolarization is a collective, all-or-none decision: different reagents give different incidences in a cohort (e.g. 70% converted), but each animal is either fully converted or fully normal; a computational model fitted to these incidences predicted interventions (two drugs and a dominant-negative construct) that were then confirmed to produce the first partially converted animals.
quote: Using different reagents could induce different incidences of hyperpigmentation (conversion) in a cohort of animals, but this was a population-level phenotype: for example, 70% of the animals could be converted, but any given animal was either fully converted or fully normal (Fig. 4a, b).
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction › From normal melanocytes to a melanoma phenotype: a collective decision
scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles with perturbed instructor-cell bioelectric signalling

label: Head-versus-tail choice at a planarian cut cannot be made locally
claim: When a planarian is cut once, cells that were adjacent neighbours at the same positional-information value make a head on one side and a tail on the other, so this anatomical decision cannot be made locally: wound cells must coordinate with the rest of the fragment to learn where they are, which way they face and what structures remain.
quote: In other words, it is actually impossible for an anatomical decision like this to be made locally – the cells of the wound must coordinate with the remaining fragment to get information about where they are located, which way they are facing, and what other structures exist121,122, in order to make adaptive decisions about large-scale growth and form that enable regeneration of normal worms.
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions
scope: Regenerating planarian fragments

label: Cryptic planaria randomize head number per animal, not per cell
claim: Perturbing the planarian bioelectric control circuit produces 'Cryptic' destabilized worms whose fragments, even from the same parent, regenerate one-headed and two-headed forms at a set frequency of about 1:2, yet each animal has clear heads and tails rather than mixed tissue, so the randomized bioelectric state is interpreted by collectives rather than by individual cells.
quote: More specifically, several perturbations targeting the bioelectric control circuit (Fig. 5e) have shown randomization of outcome: such Cryptic planaria are destabilized, and fragments (even from the same parent worm) will form 1-head and 2-head forms at a set frequency of ~1:2130 (Fig. 5f).
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions
scope: Planarians after gap-junction or bioelectric perturbation

label: Left-right randomization is concordant within an embryo except after VANGL knockdown
claim: Bioelectric and biochemical perturbations of vertebrate left-right patterning randomize laterality only at the level of whole embryos (each embryo's cells agree on L and R identity); the only known perturbation that breaks this concordance is down-regulation of planar-polarity VANGL signalling, which produces speckled L/R marker expression on both sides of the midline.
quote: In all of the many studies on perturbation of the LR pathway, we are aware of only one that actually breaks the concordance: disruption of the planar polarity pathway by down-regulating VANGL signaling149 leads to a speckling on both sides of the midline, consistent with individual cells within a single lateral domain disagreeing on whether they should have L or R identity (Fig. 6a–d).
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction › Left/right, head/tail: random, but collective anatomical decisions
scope: Vertebrate embryos (chick, Xenopus and others) with perturbed left-right pathways

label: Grafted groups of neural crest cells keep their identity; single grafted cells do not
claim: Single neural crest cells transposed to a different anterior-posterior axial domain change their gene expression to match their neighbours, whereas groups of transposed cells keep their original gene expression, which the authors interpret as collectives having greater positional memory (a perceptual field extending further into the past) than individual cells.
quote: Individual cells transposed from one anterior-posterior axial domain to another will change their gene expression to match their neighbors159,161,162. In contrast, groups of cells transposed along the anterior-posterior axis maintain their original gene expression, thus resisting the inductive effects of the surrounding tissue159,161,162.
paper_title: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates
section: Introduction › Neural crest intelligence is collective
scope: Vertebrate neural crest (chick, mouse) transplantation
